spec.description: Legacy cancel-replace edit of a live order's parameters: the original order is cancelled and a new order is created with the adjusted parameters, returning a new `order_id`. Superseded by `amend_order`, which resolves this endpoint's caveats and performs better: triggered stop-loss/take-profit orders are not supported; orders with attached conditional close terms are not supported; an edit whose executed volume exceeds the newly supplied volume is rejected; `cl_ord_id` is not supported; existing executions stay associated with the original order rather than copying to the edited one; and queue position is not maintained.

request.title: EditOrderParams
request.description: Parameters for the legacy cancel-replace edit: the original order is cancelled and a new order created with the adjusted parameters, returning a new `order_id`. Superseded by `amend_order`, which resolves this endpoint's caveats (see notes) and performs better.

order_id.description: Kraken identifier for the order to edit, e.g. `OFGKYQ-FHPCQ-HUQFEK`.

symbol.description: Original symbol identifier for the pair, e.g. `BTC/USD`. The symbol cannot be amended.

order_qty.description: Order quantity in terms of the base asset.

display_qty.description: For iceberg orders only: quantity to show in the book while the rest of `order_qty` remains hidden. Minimum value is 1/15 of `order_qty`.

limit_price.description: Limit price, for order types that support a limit price restriction.

fee_preference.description: Fee preference, base or quote currency. `quote` is the default for buy orders, `base` is the default for sell orders.

no_mpp.description: Deprecated -- if supplied, accepted but ignored. Was: disable Market Price Protection for market orders.

order_userref.description: User-defined reference to place on the edited order. Does not identify the order to be edited -- use `order_id` for that.

post_only.description: Cancels the order if it would take liquidity on arrival. For orders with a limit price only.

reduce_only.description: Reduces an existing margin position without opening an opposite position worth more than the current value of the leveraged assets.

triggers.title: EditOrderTriggers
triggers.description: Trigger price conditions for triggered order types.

reference.description: Reference price to track for triggering orders: `index` (the broader-market index price for this pair -- falls back to `last` during index-feed connectivity issues) or `last` (the last traded price in the Kraken order book for this pair).

price.description: Amount for the trigger price -- static or relative, per `price_type`. E.g. 29000.5 with `price_type=static` triggers at that price; 5 with `pct` triggers when price rises 5%; -150 with `quote` triggers when price drops 150 quote-currency units. For `trailing-stop`/`trailing-stop-limit`, represents the reversion from the peak price and is always positive.

price_type.description: Units for `price`: `static` (a static market price), `pct` (a percentage offset from the reference price), or `quote` (a notional offset in the quote currency).

validate.description: If `true`, the edit is validated only -- it never reaches the matching engine.

deadline.description: RFC3339 timestamp, millisecond precision. Valid offsets from the current time range from 500ms to 60s (default 5s). The engine will not match this order after this time.

response.title: EditOrderResultFrame
response.description: Wire frame; the generated method returns `result`.

method.description: Wire envelope field; see the core.

req_id.description: Wire envelope field; see the core.

order_id.description: Unique ID of the new (edited) order.

original_order_id.description: ID of the original order that was edited.

warnings.description: Non-fatal warnings about the edit, if any.

success.description: Wire envelope field; see the core.

time_in.description: Wire envelope field; see the core.

time_out.description: Wire envelope field; see the core.

notes: `token` (the auth bearer token) is documented by Kraken as a required params field but is deliberately absent from this schema: `core/transport/ws.py`'s `SocketConnection.rpc_send` merges the cached token into every outgoing `params` on the private connection -- trading calls and subscribe/unsubscribe alike -- so it is transport-injected, never a caller-supplied argument, the same way `req_id` (the declared `correlate` field) never appears in a requestBody schema. Kept in scope despite being legacy/superseded by `amend_order`, since discovery.md and core.md both list it as a live v2 trading method. `triggers.price` is not `required` here (unlike `add_order`'s/`batch_add`'s `OrderTriggers`, where it is), per the doc page's own field markup -- hence the separate `EditOrderTriggers` title rather than reusing `OrderTriggers`.

Deliberately left as a flat request body (production_standards.md S12), not a `requestBody`/`anyOf` discriminated union like `add_order`/`batch_add`: unlike those, an edit-by-id request carries no `order_type` field at all to discriminate on -- the edit targets an existing order by `order_id`, and Kraken's wire contract for this endpoint provides no local field whose value would select which variant's required-field profile applies. Building an `anyOf` here would mean inventing a discriminant the venue doesn't provide, which authoring rule 2's "never invent" bar rules out just as much for a discriminant as for an enum value.
